applicability.jurisdiction_or_standard_context: Fraia product-architecture card informed by public structural analysis and solver documentation. Not a design-code rule.

claims.text: Finite element analysis represents a continuum or structure through discrete elements connected at nodes.

source_refs.locator: OpenSees Elastic Beam Column Element documentation

claims.text: A frame or beam-column element is a solver-level analysis object with element connectivity, transformation, and section or stiffness inputs.

source_refs.locator: Applications of the direct stiffness method

claims.text: Fraia should keep an authored member such as a beam, column, or rafter distinct from any one or more analysis elements used to realize it for calculation.

limitations: This card defines a Fraia modeling distinction; external sources support the analysis-element concept, not Fraia's internal object names.
A single authored member may map to one or many analysis elements depending on releases, segmentation, meshing, and solver requirements.

pages_used: Applications of the direct stiffness method

summary: Fraia should distinguish user-authored structural members from solver-level analysis elements so results and explanations preserve provenance.
title: Authored Member And Analysis Element Separation
